title: Cello bow crosses the strings

source.why_this_clip: A cellist seen from the front plays an upright cello, drawing the bow across the strings while her left hand moves on the neck. The clip has no cuts; this last stretch is after the caption bar has gone and the camera shows more of the cello body than the earlier frames.

source_selection.evidence: Sixteen raw samples show the samecellist bowing in one continuous close shot with caption absent. No cut/dissolve inside18.25–20.75. Retained endpoint slightly shortened to the final frozen vector observation; no pose extrapolation.

assembly_summary: Five native cello strokes preserve body, neck, strings and fholes. Agent-drawn bow and moving hand are separately credited; instrument and lower bow remain cropped like source. The simplified held player edges do not assert a full-body performance reconstruction. A separately credited pale foreground player contour now supports the neck hand through observed shoulder/elbow positions.
review_note: Bounded v2 after blind operation review: minimum pale source-observed player/head/shoulder/left-arm contours connect the existing neck hand through its changing elbow support. Original cello and bow/crop unchanged. Fresh review pending; no actual normal-speed approval or training.
